title: Application to Zodiac (remote graphical RAG companion + web crawlers)
keyFindings: Graph RAG is the core of Zodiac's design, not an optional enhancement: Zodiac's contract already requires pre-graphing + vector-embedding of web-crawled data (zodiac.md §4.2) and graph/vector/hybrid query modes (§4.3.2), which are exactly the knowledge-graph-from-web-crawl and graph-enhanced-vector-search patterns.

Zodiac's hybrid mode (§4.3.2) is graph-enhanced vector search (HybridRAG); the merge/ranking algorithm is unpinned and should be specified (RRF-style rank fusion or weighted combination) as a proposed spec change.

The advanced Graph RAG techniques — dynamic graph query generation (text-to-graph for the `graph` mode), parent-child retrievers (crawl → chunk hierarchy), graph enrichments (entity resolution/dedup of crawled packages), and explainability traces (source path per result) — are all proposed spec changes, none currently pinned in zodiac.md.

Dependency-graph RAG is a named, web-grounded pattern (DepsRAG) that maps directly onto Zodiac's dependency-package domain, enabling relationship and multi-hop queries ('what depends on X?') that flat vector RAG cannot answer.

Graph RAG is fully D1/D2-compatible: the techniques are open algorithms (AGPL-3.0-safe) and run locally (LightRAG, GraphRAG-with-Ollama), so the remote-by-design Zodiac (D2-CLARIFICATION) and the local-first suite both satisfy the constraints.
Every graph-query capability must be reachable through both the GUI and the MCP surface (zodiac_query, rag_query/rag_stream) to satisfy D4; a graph feature on only one surface is a D4 violation.
summary: Graph RAG is the core mechanism of Zodiac (a remote graphical RAG companion that pre-graphs and vector-embeds web-crawled data) and a first-class capability of Astrographer, whose documents are already Provident graphs. The MUST tier confirms Zodiac's existing pre-graphing + hybrid-mode contract and directs pinning the unpinned merge/ranking and graph-query semantics; the advanced techniques (dynamic graph query generation, parent-child retrievers, graph enrichments, explainability traces, community summaries) are SHOULD/NICE-TO-HAVE proposed spec changes. The techniques are open, local-first implementable, and interconnection-serving, satisfying D1-D4.
